Blue note reading approximately 'Tunnel shaft fractured, unable... to proceed' - the first mention of the mechanical failure that leads to the ship's extended Madras layup a few weeks later. Position on the card suggests this was first identified around the Aden call
UNCERTAIN - red = sailing, carried forward from Aden; exact date reconstructed from the top reference line rather than a clearly legible bottom-line citation

MAJOR INCIDENT - blue note reads 'Put into Madras 18/10 with tunnel shaft fractured', dated '(Lo.) 24/10'. This begins a nearly four-month layup: the card logs a long run of 'in port'/ditto citations confirming the ship remained at Madras without moving - 4/11/1943, 15/11/1943, 2/12/1943, 13/12/1943, 20/12/1943, 3/1/1944, 20/1/1944, and 3/2/1944 (each marked 'Madras -|-' or 'in pt', i.e. still there) - the longest layup logged anywhere in this collection. A further blue note reads approximately '9/2/44, re cargo' - context (what cargo, why noted) not established
black = arrival - the ship finally moves again, after nearly four months at Madras
Two ditto marks ('-|- -|-') follow, indicating the ship remained at Calcutta for a period before the next dated citation
